title: The Institute of Policy Studies called for private investment, productivity and competitive exports to drive the next phase of growth.
body_paragraphs: The think-tank’s annual report said the recovery must avoid reopening fiscal and external vulnerabilities that caused the 2022 crisis. It pointed to two consecutive years of 5% real GDP growth in 2024 and 2025 and 4.7% in the first half of 2026 as a platform for reform.

It warned that two‑thirds of workers were in informal jobs and urged labour‑market changes to raise job quality and skills. The report also put resilience to climate and energy shocks at the centre of policy, calling for investment in renewables, food systems and disaster preparedness.

title: Youth unemployment reached 17.8% in the second quarter, with the rate among young women at 22.4%.
body_paragraphs: Official survey data counted 150,684 jobseekers aged 15 to 24 and put overall joblessness at 4%, or 340,240 people. The same release showed the 25–29 age group at 12.1%, with a gap of 19.7% for women versus 7.7% for men.

Labour-force participation was 50%, split between 70.3% for men and 32.7% for women. Among those with G.C.E. Advanced Level or higher, unemployment stood at 6.7% compared with lower average rates for less-educated groups.

title: The Government decided to retain ownership of the East Container Terminal while bringing private investors into a new operating company.
body_paragraphs: The Cabinet move followed concerns that the facility handled roughly 500,000 boxes against a capacity near 3.2 million. The head of state also said a breakwater for a second phase at the western terminal would cost about $1.4 billion, up from an earlier $1.1 billion estimate.

An interim feasibility report is due in December from a multilateral lender, with a final version expected in April. Funds will be set aside in the upcoming Budget to advance preparatory work on the expansion.

title: Solar firms warned that a policy shift to compulsory Net Plus and shorter contracts could raise bills and deter rooftop investment.
body_paragraphs: Industry representatives said paying households about Rs. 13,000 for 550 units exported while charging Rs. 47,000–48,000 for the same usage would erode returns. They urged the regulator to reinstate Net Metering and Net Accounting, expand storage and smart‑grid upgrades, and adopt battery energy storage systems (BESS, grid‑scale batteries that absorb surplus generation).

Trade bodies said more than 2,600 MW of rooftop capacity now displaces imported fuels and supports over 21,000 jobs across 800 firms. They called for independence in tariff reviews and targeted transformer upgrades to integrate daytime generation.

title: The IMF (International Monetary Fund) said it stood ready to support the country beyond the current programme.
body_paragraphs: A senior official praised stronger fiscal performance and noted that debt restructuring was largely complete. The seventh review at staff level envisaged about $345 million in disbursements, subject to Board approval.

title: The Central Bank defended the 5% inflation target even as headline price growth rose to 8% in September.
body_paragraphs: Officials argued a lower anchor would have forced sharper rate hikes and weaker nominal GDP, straining debt ratios. They said peers took “10 to 25 years” to shift from 5–8% to 2–3% targets and warned disinflation carried output costs.

title: Customs surpassed its full‑year revenue goal of Rs. 2,207 billion by October 13.
body_paragraphs: Collections reached Rs. 2,208 billion, nearly a month earlier than last year’s milestone. The agency cited tighter enforcement and said digital signatures for declarations would become compulsory from October 19.

title: Vehicle registrations climbed 18.3% in September to 54,214 units, led by two‑wheelers and three‑wheelers.
body_paragraphs: Two‑wheeler volumes rose to 38,747 and three‑wheelers to 5,375, together accounting for just over 81% of the total. Electric entries reached 6,048 units, with about 83% from two‑wheelers, while brand‑new and pre‑owned small cars dominated passenger sales.

title: The Court of Appeal ordered authorities to take measures to reduce train–elephant collisions and report back in three months.
body_paragraphs: In a public‑interest case, the bench issued writs directing wildlife officials to prepare management plans and the rail operator to detail training, simulators and speed regulation at crossings. The ruling also recognised a surviving elephant as a petitioner represented by a next friend.

title: The Saudi Supreme Court set aside a death sentence on a Sri Lankan national after a joint legal and diplomatic effort.
body_paragraphs: The decision removed capital punishment imposed earlier by an appellate court and followed filings by local and Saudi counsel. The Government said it would cover legal expenses and continue assisting the family until remaining proceedings conclude.
